subject: Recap & next steps: token economics scenarios + model routing decision
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Park <susan@autonexus.com>, Devin Morris <devin.morris@autonexus.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps: token economics scenarios + model routing decision

Hi Susan / Devin —

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to meet the Autonexus team. Below is a short recap of what we heard, a set of simple token-econ scenarios (high/medium/low), and a suggestion for an initial model routing mix to validate over the pilot. Would love to lock the preferred target $/1M tokens so we can convert these into a formal pilot proposal and SOW.

Quick recap (from your notes):
- Primary surface: in-product summarization + 1:1 assistant.
- Volume expectation: bursty signals, ~10M–50M tokens/month in steady-state; pilot window target of 1–3M tokens.
- Data sensitivity: PII in prompts, requires SOC2 evidence and VPC option for production.

Three simple token-econ scenarios (all $ per 1M tokens):
1) Conservative (accuracy-first) — $1,200 / 1M tokens — Model mix: 70% chat-large (high-quality), 25% chat-medium, 5% rerank/embeds for retrieval.
2) Balanced (cost/quality) — $750 / 1M tokens — Model mix: 50% chat-medium, 30% chat-small, 15% embeddings (for retrieval), 5% rerank.
3) Cost-optimised — $420 / 1M tokens — Model mix: 40% chat-small (quantized), 40% embeddings for heavy retrieval, 20% rerank + lightweight chat for control.

Assumptions and footnotes:
- Estimates include typical prefix caching and batching benefits we can enable on pilot traffic.
- Embeddings priced per 1M embedding-units; converted here to token-equivalent for rough comparison.
- If you need guaranteed latency SLAs we’ll recommend Dedicated capacity (adds ~15–25% to unit price).

Suggested next steps / asks from Autonexus:
- Confirm which scenario aligns with your business target (pick one or give a target $/1M tokens).
- Share a short sample prompt traffic profile (anonymized) so we can run a better estimate.
- If procurement is required, flag primary contact and any standard PO/SLA terms.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.pdf (draft timeline & responsibilities).

I’ll follow up with a short XLS with the token scenarios broken down per-model and sensitivity ranges.

Best,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Susan Park <susan@autonexus.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Devin Morris <devin.morris@autonexus.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: token economics scenarios + model routing decision

Thanks Marcus — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifying items before we pick a scenario:  
1) For the Balanced option, what do you mean by chat-medium vs chat-small (are these different model families or quantization tiers)?
2) How do embeddings factor into cost if we plan to do an incremental update of our vector DB (daily sync) — is there an additional per-record cost?

Also procurement wants to understand the expected pilot duration and whether the pilot cap can limit spend. Devin, can you confirm procurement cadence?

Appreciate the attachment — looking forward to the XLS.

—Susan
Susan Park
Head of Product — Autonexus
susan@autonexus.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Park <susan@autonexus.com>, Devin Morris <devin.morris@autonexus.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: token economics scenarios + model routing decision

Susan — great questions. High level answers and attached XLS contains line-item math.

1) chat-medium vs chat-small:
- chat-medium = a mid-tier chat model (larger context, higher per-token compute) — used where user-facing replies need higher coherence (e.g., multi-turn assistant).
- chat-small = compact/quantized variant (lower compute) — good for short completions or system messages where latency/cost matters.

2) Embeddings:
- We charge embeddings per 1M embedding units; for your incremental daily sync the cost depends on documents/records processed. For your 200k-candidate dataset doing daily incremental embeddings (assume 2k records changed/day) the marginal cost is low — we included representative embedding volume in the Balanced and Cost-optimised scenarios.

Attached: redwood_token_scenarios.xlsx — it includes three tabs: ScenarioSummary, PerModelBreakdown, Sensitivity (±20% token volume). Key excerpts below:

Per-model breakdown (Balanced scenario; per 1M total tokens):
- chat-medium: 500,000 tokens -> $380
- chat-small: 300,000 tokens -> $180
- embeddings (converted equivalent): 150,000 tokens -> $160
- rerank: 50,000 tokens -> $30
Total: $750 / 1M tokens (as indicated).

Pilot guardrails we can offer:
- Fixed pilot cap (e.g., $5k–$15k) — we can hard quota the trial account to stop at cap.
- Weekly usage alerts and token-level dashboards in Redwood Console.
- Option for a 30-day pilot and a one-time credit applied if you commit to a Reserved/Dedicated contract within 90 days.

Ask: can you confirm your preferred unit target (pick one of our scenarios or provide target $/1M tokens)? If you pick Balanced, we’ll bake the PerModelBreakdown into the SOW/MP and return a draft SOW.

Thanks — attaching XLS.

Best,
Marcus

Attachment: redwood_token_scenarios.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Recap & next steps: token economics scenarios + model routing decision

Team — forwarding the Autonexus thread. They look like a Balanced or Cost-optimised buyer but product prefers the Balanced mix for quality. A few internal items:  
- Price floor: we should be comfortable at $600 / 1M for a pilot-stage agreement for a 3-month pilot if we can show hit rates on fidelity.
- SLA ask: they may push for SOC2 + VPC for production — Monica, confirm lead-time for Private deployment (we have a standard 6–8 week window for first VPC install).
- Discounts: we can offer pilot credits (10–20%) and tie step-up to Reserved commitment.

If you have redlines on per-model pricing or have a recommended conservative fallback profile, drop it here.

—Marcus

From: Autonexus Procurement <procurement@autonexus.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Susan Park <susan@autonexus.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: SOW request & redlines: pilot cap and PO info

Hi Marcus / Susan —

Thanks for the details. Procurement is comfortable with a 30-day pilot and a not-to-exceed pilot cap of $12,000. Please send a draft SOW that:
- Aligns to the Balanced scenario pricing (we prefer cost/quality balance).
- Includes a clause on pilot cap and a clear escalation path for production SLA and VPC deployment.
- States the estimated time-to-prod (if we sign Reserved/Dedicated) and the dependencies.

Attached: Autonexus_SOW_draft.docx (procurement template) — please return a redlined SOW by EOD Friday.

Procurement contact: Devin Morris <devin.morris@autonexus.com>

Regards,
Autonexus Procurement
procurement@autonexus.com
